# Data visualization
Start with the question, source, units, aggregation, and time period. Reconcile totals and signs. Show missing, stale, estimated, and partial data clearly.

Choose the simplest chart or table that explains the comparison. Static charts are appropriate when interaction adds no value. Inspection and filtering should serve a real task.

Use clear labels, suitable scales, color-independent meaning, and text or table alternatives when useful. Keep styling consistent with the surrounding product or publication.

Verify plotted values against data and inspect the rendered result. Document material limitations and avoid inferring causation from timing alone.
